newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: ICRC condemns attack in Chechnya, names victims.
newsitem.headline: ICRC condemns attack in Chechnya, names victims.

text.p: The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) on Tuesday condemned what it called the "cold-blooded" murder of six of its Western staff by unidentified gunmen in Chechnya.

In a statement, ICRC confirmed it was withdrawing its 14 remaining delegates from Novye Atagi, south of Grozny, later in the day, and named the six victims and Swiss national in charge of the office, who also received gunshot wounds in the attack.
"The ICRC is profoundly shocked and grieved by this tragedy and vigorously condemns this attack and the violation of the Red Cross emblem," the Swiss-run humanitarian agency said.
"Six of its delegates were cold-bloodedly shot dead this morning by unidentified gunmen at their quarters at the hospital in Novye Atagi, near Grozny, at 4 a.m. local time," it said.

The ICRC expressed its deepest sympathy to the families of the deceased, "who gave their lives to help the victims of the Chechen conflict", and to the Red Cross Societies of the Netherlands, Norway, Canada and New Zealand.

It named the six, shot in their beds at their quarters at the hospital compound, as: Hans Elkerbout (construction technician, Netherlands Red Cross), Ingeborg Foss (nurse, Norwegian Red Cross), Nancy Malloy (medical administrator, Canadian Red Cross), Gunnhild Myklebust (nurse, Norwegian Red Cross) and Sheryl Thayer (nurse, New Zealand Red Cross) and Fernanda Calado, a Spanish nurse under contract to the ICRC. Christophe Hensch was the Swiss in charge who survived.
